claims.text: Data ownership: each kind of data has exactly one owner, the service or module that writes it and whose value counts when copies disagree; every other place holds a copy.
claims.source_hint: glossary data-ownership; outline item 1; docs/design/data-ownership.md @ stage-4 lines 3-6

claims.text: Owners at stage-4: Catalog owns products, Ordering owns orders and customers, Payments owns payments (donhang_payments), Notifications owns the emails to send (donhang_notifications), Keycloak owns the sign-in accounts.
The Redis copy of a product is deleted after a price change and lives at most 5 minutes (TTL) even if the delete is missed.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/data-ownership.md @ stage-4 line 13; DonHang.Catalog/ProductCache.cs @ stage-4 (Ttl = 5 min, UpdatePriceAsync deletes the key)

claims.text: customerEmail (and customerName) in each order.* message (every message whose routing key starts with order., such as order.placed) is copied when written to the outbox and on purpose never updated; when values differ, customers is trusted.

The old payments table in donhang: its rows were copied into donhang_payments at the split (ADR 0003); its rule is that nothing updates it, kept only until accounting confirms (ADR 0008); payments made after the split exist only in donhang_payments.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/data-ownership.md @ stage-4 line 15; STAGE.md @ stage-4 lines 21-25 (old payments table stays, debt N2)

claims.text: order_items.unit_price_vnd is not a copy of the product's price but the price the customer paid, a fact of the order, deliberately not changed by a new price; Order.Total is worked out from the items' prices each time it is read.

claims.text: ADR 0008 drops the old payments table only after accounting confirms its check against donhang_payments; accounting objected to dropping it at once: they check old payments each quarter end and had not yet checked the rows copied into donhang_payments.

Rule for shared writes: never let both write; give the data one owner and let the other ask it by a call or a message. Example: Payments does not change an order's status; it publishes payment.refunded and the API, owner of orders, changes it.
Payments keeps only an order_id, a plain number with no foreign key to orders.
Order.CompleteRefund accepts the change only when the status is refunding; while a refund is under way the order shows refunding until payment.refunded is handled.

The owner's value counts whichever changed last; a price set by hand in the Redis copy goes back to the products value once the key is deleted (e.g. next price change); writing the key with SET without giving a TTL discards its previous TTL, so the wrong copy stays until then.
claims.source_hint: Redis docs, SET command (previous TTL discarded on successful SET); DonHang.Catalog/ProductCache.cs @ stage-4 lines 54-59, 90; data-ownership.md @ stage-4 line 13

claims.text: Trade-offs: asking the owner by a call gives the current value but fails while the owner is unreachable; a copy with a rule is as old as its rule allows; a fact of a record never follows later changes; letting two places write is needed by no operation in Đơn Hàng.
claims.source_hint: Outline items 3 and 6; docs/design/data-ownership.md @ stage-4 lines 11-36

claims.text: If a wrong amount is found on an old payment, correct it in donhang_payments through Payments rather than in the old payments table, because that table is a copy nobody updates.
When a second service wants to set orders.status, keep the payment.refunded message rather than a second writer; the cost is eventual consistency.
order_status_history is a read model written in the same transaction as the order by RecordOrderStatusHistory.
